From 1822 to 1844 Haiti ruled the whole island of Hispaniola, after President Jean-Pierre Boyer marched into Santo Domingo. The eastern part had just declared a short lived independence from Spain.

Boyer abolished slavery in the east and redistributed land. But the Haitian state also closed the university, took church lands and taxed the east to pay the independence debt, and many Spanish speaking families left.

In 1844 the secret society La Trinitaria of Juan Pablo Duarte led the war of independence. Dominicans count their nationhood from breaking with Haiti, not Spain, which has coloured relations between the two countries ever since.
